index.html.description: Ship secure API platforms with Apigee X. Four hands-on training tracks cover open banking, FAPI, Spring Boot bridge, and AI Gateway from foundational to advanced.

fapi-30-day/day-01.html.description: Learn Apigee X architecture: control plane, runtime plane, environments, proxy endpoints, and how requests flow from client through runtime to backend.

fapi-30-day/day-02.html.description: Provision a free Apigee X evaluation organization on Google Cloud and install apigeecli for managing proxies, deployments, and API products.

fapi-30-day/day-03.html.description: Build a reverse-proxy bundle with manifest, ProxyEndpoint, TargetEndpoint files and deploy to your Apigee environment using apigeecli.

fapi-30-day/day-04.html.description: Master conditional flows per HTTP method and path, understand the request/response pipeline, and route to different backends with RouteRules.

fapi-30-day/day-05.html.description: Learn the universal policy pattern: XML files plus Step attachments to flows, starting with AssignMessage to build and modify responses.

fapi-30-day/day-06.html.description: Protect backends with Quota for business limits, SpikeArrest for burst smoothing, and ConcurrentRateLimit for simultaneous call caps.

fapi-30-day/day-07.html.description: Extract values from requests with ExtractVariables and reshape messages with AssignMessage Set/Add/Copy/Remove for mediation in both directions.

fapi-30-day/day-08.html.description: Write JavaScript policies for complex transformation logic and use message templates with built-in functions for dynamic values without code.

fapi-30-day/day-09.html.description: Call secondary services mid-flow with ServiceCallout and decouple backend hostnames from your bundle using environment-specific TargetServers.

fapi-30-day/day-10.html.description: Reduce latency with ResponseCache for reference data, cache computed values with LookupCache/PopulateCache, and store config in Key Value Maps.

fapi-30-day/day-11.html.description: Handle faults in Apigee with RaiseFault, FaultRules, and DefaultFaultRule. Build an OBIE error taxonomy for validation, rate-limit, and unexpected failures.

fapi-30-day/day-12.html.description: Build shared flows and attach via FlowCallout or flow hooks to centralize FAPI headers and errors. Enforce cross-cutting policy across proxies, no copy-paste.

fapi-30-day/day-13.html.description: Model app identity with developers, apps, and API products; gate with VerifyAPIKey. Bind product quotas so plan changes skip redeploy, the governance unit.

fapi-30-day/day-14.html.description: Issue OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens via GenerateAccessToken (client-credentials grant); protect resources with VerifyAccessToken. Give TPPs short-lived credentials.

fapi-30-day/day-15.html.description: Implement authorization-code + PKCE and mint/verify JWTs with GenerateJWT and VerifyJWT. Prevent code interception with S256 and sign id_tokens for user flows.

fapi-30-day/day-16.html.description: Secure proxy edges with keystores and truststores; add mTLS for backends. Use references for zero-downtime rotation and expose client certs for FAPI binding.

fapi-30-day/day-17.html.description: Block malformed JSON and injection with threat protection, enable CORS safely for browser TPPs, mask PII in traces/logs. Centralize defenses in shared flows.

fapi-30-day/day-18.html.description: Learn the FAPI 1.0 Advanced 12-point checklist: PAR, PS256 request objects, private_key_jwt auth, cert-bound tokens, JARM. Map each to Apigee mechanisms.

fapi-30-day/day-19.html.description: Build the FAPI authorization server: PAR endpoint with PS256 request-object checks, private_key_jwt client auth, and cert-bound tokens per resource access.

fapi-30-day/day-20.html.description: Map the UK Open Banking ecosystem: ASPSP (bank), TPP roles (AISP/PISP), PSU consent, Directory, SSA, and OBWAC (mTLS) vs OBSEAL (signing) certificates.

fapi-30-day/day-21.html.description: Build the account-access consent lifecycle on Apigee: create consents, bind them to PSU authorization, enforce status and permissions on every data call.

fapi-30-day/day-22.html.description: Expose OBIE account information APIs secured by consent permission checks: shape core responses into Data/Links/Meta envelopes with pagination.

fapi-30-day/day-23.html.description: Build payment-initiation APIs with two-step consent, detached JWS signature verification, idempotency, immutable initiation and funds checks.

fapi-30-day/day-24.html.description: Auto-onboard TPPs at scale with Dynamic Client Registration: verify Directory-signed SSAs as a trust anchor, cache TPP JWKS, complete certificate-bound tokens.

fapi-30-day/day-25.html.description: Assemble a production-ready Open Banking proxy estate: shared security flows, MECE decomposition by concern, flow hooks for governance, and conformance.

fapi-30-day/day-26.html.description: Promote identical proxy revisions across test and prod: route by hostname via environment groups, externalize all config into TargetServers and KVMs.

fapi-30-day/day-27.html.description: Automate proxy delivery with GitHub Actions: lint and deploy to test, run API contract tests, gate production promotion with four-eyes review.

fapi-30-day/day-28.html.description: Master four observability lenses: Analytics for trends, Cloud Logging for audit trails, Cloud Trace for latency attribution, Debug for live troubleshooting.

fapi-30-day/day-29.html.description: Package proxies into API products and publish on a developer portal: attach OpenAPI specs, optional monetization, and catalog everything in API hub.

fapi-30-day/day-30.html.description: Execute production-readiness review: performance budgets, multi-region failover, security hardening checklist, operations runbooks, compliance audit trail.

fapi-30-day/index.html.description: Go from zero to shipping a FAPI-secured UK Open Banking API on Apigee X: master OAuth, mTLS, JWS/JWT, consent, and API proxy development with hands-on labs.

spring-boot-devs/index.html.description: Master Apigee X across 33 sessions that map every concept to Spring Boot. Learn FAPI, Open Banking, and production APIs with hands-on labs in your eval org.

spring-boot-devs/session-01.html.description: Learn what separates API management from a basic gateway: the 80% around the proxy—consumers, analytics, publishing, lifecycle, and policy-based control.

spring-boot-devs/session-02.html.description: Understand Apigee X's control plane and runtime architecture. Map the org-environment-group-instance hierarchy and provision a free evaluation org for labs.

spring-boot-devs/session-03.html.description: Author and deploy your first Apigee proxy in XML, then call it via curl. This passthrough reverse proxy proves your entire control-plane-to-backend stack end to end.

spring-boot-devs/session-04.html.description: Manage proxy revisions as immutable artifacts. Deploy changes, roll back safely, and prove both with curl: deploy is a cheap pointer move, not a rebuild.

spring-boot-devs/session-05.html.description: Debug Apigee proxies with the Trace tool: see every policy execute in order, watch flow variables at each step, and pinpoint exactly where requests go wrong.

spring-boot-devs/session-06.html.description: Discover the flow model: two endpoints and four attach points where policies run. Grasp ProxyEndpoint and TargetEndpoint separation, the base of every proxy.

spring-boot-devs/session-07.html.description: Master the flow-variable namespace: request, response, system, client, custom. Policies share typed, request-scoped variables across four attach points.

spring-boot-devs/session-08.html.description: Route and branch with conditions over flow variables. Build conditional flows and RouteRules, a config-driven alternative to controller if/switch logic.

spring-boot-devs/session-09.html.description: Extract path segments, query params, headers, and JSON fields into variables. Reshape requests and responses with AssignMessage to replace custom code.

spring-boot-devs/session-20.html.description: Learn the four Open Banking roles (ASPSP, AISP, PISP, CBPII) and the OB Directory trust model. Validate TPP certificates and enforce the regulated framework.

spring-boot-devs/session-21.html.description: Understand FAPI Advanced as hardened OAuth: nine independent clauses from PAR to JARM, each mapped to an Apigee policy. Build your implementation checklist.

spring-boot-devs/session-22.html.description: Implement FAPI PAR: verify signed request objects with VerifyJWT, authenticate clients with private_key_jwt, and store requests by request_uri for authorize.

spring-boot-devs/session-23.html.description: Make tokens sender-constrained by stamping certificate thumbprints (cnf.x5t#S256) at issuance. Enforce binding on every call and expose RFC 7662 introspection.

spring-boot-devs/session-24.html.description: Implement automated client registration: validate the Software Statement from the OB Directory, auto-provision a developer app, and return client_id per RFC 7591.

spring-boot-devs/session-25.html.description: Model account-access consent as a state machine (AwaitingAuthorisation → Authorised → Revoked). Persist state in a KVM and gate every read on consent status.

spring-boot-devs/session-26.html.description: Implement consent-scoped AISP reads by enforcing three checks: token scope, Authorised consent status, and requested account in the consent set.

spring-boot-devs/session-27.html.description: Guard domestic payments with x-idempotency-key: cache the first submission, replay it on retry, and prevent duplicate money movement via gateway dedup.

spring-boot-devs/session-28.html.description: Implement Confirmation of Funds (CBPII) with one boolean response and privacy-by-design, then orchestrate the end-to-end journey: consent, read, pay, confirm.

spring-boot-devs/session-29.html.description: Promote one immutable revision across environments: let TargetServers and KVMs differ per environment so dev and test talk to different backends from one bundle.

spring-boot-devs/session-30.html.description: Treat Apigee config as code: lint bundles with apigeelint, build revisions with apigeecli, deploy via CI/CD, and authenticate runners with Workload Identity.

spring-boot-devs/session-31.html.description: Measure API traffic automatically with Apigee Analytics, stream logs to Cloud Logging, trace requests with Cloud Trace, and detect abuse with Advanced API Security.

spring-boot-devs/session-32.html.description: Bundle API operations into products for self-service: publish OpenAPI specs to dev portals, enable key registration, attach rate plans, govern with API hub.

spring-boot-devs/session-33.html.description: Assemble a regulated Open Banking platform from DCR, consent, AISP, PISP, and CoF operations behind FAPI and mTLS, then run a go-live readiness review checklist.

tetrate-ai-gateway/index.html.description: Govern LLMs and AI agents at the edge with token budgets, guardrails, and multi-provider routing across 29 sessions tied to Apigee and Spring Boot concepts.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-01.html.description: See why LLM provider calls fail at scale; every service needs a governed edge for identity, metering, budgets, guardrails, audit: why AI gateways exist.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-02.html.description: Map your Apigee knowledge onto AI gateways. Learn what transfers and the three new concepts: variable token cost, natural-language payloads, agentic state.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-03.html.description: Navigate Tetrate's product ladder: open-source Envoy AI Gateway, TARS managed endpoint, Agent Router Enterprise, Agent Operations Director. Pick your on-ramp.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-04.html.description: Make your first governed LLM call with a one-line change: swap the base URL to the gateway endpoint. Route to two vendors by changing only the model field.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-05.html.description: Self-host Envoy AI Gateway on Kubernetes with three CRDs: AIServiceBackend names the provider, BackendSecurityPolicy the credential, AIGatewayRoute the route.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-06.html.description: The OpenAI-compatible API is the lingua franca. AIServiceBackend schema.name adapts OpenAI-shaped requests to Anthropic, Bedrock, and GCP behind one contract.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-07.html.description: Move provider credentials to the gateway. BackendSecurityPolicy injects API keys and AWS SigV4 upstream, so apps hold no secrets and rotation skips redeploy.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-08.html.description: Publish a model catalog via AIGatewayRoute rules. Use virtual model names like chat-default with modelNameOverride to swap the provider, unseen by clients.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-09.html.description: Configure retry and timeout with BackendTrafficPolicy, then fail over to another model vendor when the primary degrades. Switchover keeps completions flowing.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-10.html.description: Route embeddings, multimodal, and image endpoints through your AI gateway using the same governance as chat, accounting for different token metering per call type.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-11.html.description: Implement token-based rate limiting with distributed counters at the gateway, limiting by token cost rather than request count for true AI traffic governance.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-12.html.description: Attribute AI token spend to users, teams, and applications at the edge, produce cost-per-team reports, and enforce budgets per cost center without per-service logic.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-13.html.description: Define sanctioned-model access tiers so callers reach only approved models by tier, enforcing deny-by-default entitlement without trusting client choices.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-14.html.description: Cache deterministic AI requests at the gateway to cut token spend and latency, using response, prompt, and semantic caching for safe, idempotent completions.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-15.html.description: Authenticate every AI caller at the edge with JWT, API keys, or OIDC before governance policies apply, turning spoofable headers into verified claims for budgets.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-16.html.description: Detect and block prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts at the gateway with AI guardrails before the model runs, using probabilistic pattern classification.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-17.html.description: Redact PII and sensitive data from prompts before egress to third-party providers and from gateway logs using pattern-based detection for cards, emails, and secrets.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-18.html.description: Judge model completions for unsafe content at the gateway using content-safety categories, blocking or rewriting toxic, violent, or policy-violating output.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-19.html.description: Secure the gateway-to-provider connection with upstream auth, TLS/mTLS, and an egress allow-list so the gateway reaches only approved LLM and tool backends.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-20.html.description: See how agentic traffic differs from chat: one prompt loops through many model and tool calls, scaling governance from one request to a multi-step session.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-21.html.description: Front Model Context Protocol tool servers with MCPRoute, routing agent tool calls through one governed endpoint instead of embedding raw clients into agent code.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-22.html.description: Aggregate multiple MCP tool servers behind one MCPRoute surface, using tool-name prefixing to multiplex calls and toolSelector to expose only safe subsets to agents.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-23.html.description: Gate tool calls with OAuth tokens and CEL rules, enforcing per-call authorization so agents read publicly but only privileged identities invoke write tools.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-24.html.description: Give autonomous agents a stable identity, per-agent token budgets, and step-caps so runaway loops are cut off at the gateway with 429, not unbounded cost.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-25.html.description: Wire token-usage and latency metrics plus OpenInference traces so multi-step agent runs appear as one session-level trace with per-step cost visibility.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-26.html.description: Reproduce a blocked AI request and use gateway debug to see which policy fired at which stage, then tell gateway-rejected from provider-rejected failures.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-27.html.description: Operate the gateway as config-as-code via Kubernetes Gateway API CRDs in git, run locally with aigw CLI, then promote manifests across clusters via GitOps.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-28.html.description: Set gateway SLOs, read AI cost and usage in Agent Operations Director, then ship models behind stable virtual names with canary fractions and quality gates.

tetrate-ai-gateway/session-29.html.description: Assemble the course into one governed multi-provider agent platform: auth, budgets, guardrails, routing, tools, observability, and operations as one whole.

mastery/assessments.html.description: Build a graduation banking API proxy capstone combining proxy design, security tiers, shared flows, CI/CD, and incident runbooks. Three assessment levels.

mastery/curriculum.html.description: Follow a 21-day instructor-led program with build days, security labs, operations training, and reviews. Progress from proxy fundamentals to production-grade.

mastery/day.html.description: Access individual day guides for the 21-day program with concepts, demos, hands-on labs, real-world failures, and defense exercises for core competency.

mastery/foundations.html.description: Learn REST principles, HTTP and URI standards, and the three-tier Apigee placement model. Understand where API gateway controls belong versus backends.

mastery/index.html.description: Master Apigee X through a structured 3-week program: REST and RFC foundations, hands-on labs, policy recipes, security patterns, and banking capstone project.

mastery/labs.html.description: Get starter code for Apigee X setup, proxy bundles, shared flows, Maven deployment, and test scripts. Build graduation proxy with multiple security tiers.

mastery/patterns.html.description: Choose security patterns for your API portfolio: high-tier open banking, medium-tier partner APIs, low-tier public APIs. Includes decision matrix and templates.

mastery/policies.html.description: Reference Apigee policy recipes: API key, OAuth, JWT, spike arrest, quota, JSON threat protection, and request shaping. Includes XML and best practices.

mastery/resources.html.description: Access primary sources for the curriculum: REST and RFC foundations, Google Cloud Apigee documentation, GoogleCloudPlatform samples, and OpenID FAPI specs.

spring-boot-devs/session-10.html.description: Learn when to use JavaScript policies vs Java callouts in Apigee X. Understand the trade-off between lightweight scripts and compiled JARs for custom gateway logic.

spring-boot-devs/session-11.html.description: Master distributed rate limiting in Apigee X. Understand SpikeArrest for smoothing bursts and product-scoped Quotas for enforcing API entitlements across instances.

spring-boot-devs/session-12.html.description: Choose the right data store in Apigee X: ResponseCache for TTL values, KVMs for mutable config, PropertySets for read-only bundles. Skip unnecessary databases.

spring-boot-devs/session-13.html.description: Secure your API edge with declarative threat protection, CORS policies, and data masking in Apigee X. Reject structural attacks before they reach backends.

spring-boot-devs/session-14.html.description: Build the Developer → App → API Product entitlement chain in Apigee X. Learn identity-based access control without hardcoding permissions into proxy code.

spring-boot-devs/session-15.html.description: Make Apigee X an OAuth 2.0 authorization server. Issue and verify client-credentials tokens without standing up a separate Spring Authorization Server.

spring-boot-devs/session-16.html.description: Implement OAuth authorization-code flow with PKCE and signed JWT tokens in Apigee X. Secure user-consent flows with stateless, delegated token verification.

spring-boot-devs/session-17.html.description: Configure north- and south-bound TLS/mTLS in Apigee X. Secure both API gateway edges with keystores and truststores for zero-downtime certificate rotation.

spring-boot-devs/session-18.html.description: Decouple backend hostnames from proxy bundles with TargetServers in Apigee X. Enable load balancing, health checks, and automatic failover across instances.

spring-boot-devs/session-19.html.description: Extract cross-cutting policies into reusable shared flows attached via FlowHooks in Apigee X. Build a fault taxonomy for consistent error responses.
